backlogged.summary: The unit test for the CLI message in AC-1 only greps the source of lib/commands/run.mjs for strings. It does not run the CLI. ES-1 does run the CLI, so the message path is covered end to end, but the AC-1 test itself is weak.

A --resume run that finds the program missing again at the post-merge verify stage repeats the merge and rollback each time. It is correct and consumes no round, but the merge work is redone on every resume.

A parallel run stopped by an environment failure leaves other features paused via Paused. If one of them hits a different fatal error in its current step, that error replaces the environment stop as the run's failure, so the environment reason is not reported. This edge case is not tested.

Redaction only replaces env values of 8 or more characters and only covers report messages (already tracked as B191, B196, B197 and B198). The environment stop path writes lastVerify to state unredacted, as it did before.
A program that itself exits 127 is treated as an environment stop (already tracked as B192).
Redaction does not cover a secret cut by tail() before redaction, so a trailing fragment of the secret can reach the report.
Only the report's failure messages are redacted. The blocked post_merge_verify detail (v.error) and e.lastVerify in runs/current.json keep the unredacted output.
Values shorter than 8 characters, or transformed values (base64, URL-encoded, split), are not redacted.

The redactor matches allowlist keys case-sensitively. On Windows, env keys are case-insensitive, so a differently-cased allowlisted name (e.g. 'path' vs 'PATH') would have its value redacted. This garbles the text but does not leak anything.

The failed item (the verify command string) is written to the report without redaction. It comes from config, not from the env, so it only leaks if a user writes a secret literally into verify.commands.
A verify command that exits 127 for its own reasons is treated as an environment stop, not as a round failure.
